findings.title: Production base URL is a non-existent placeholder host
findings.observed_fact: _baseUrlFor(Flavor.prod) returns 'https://TBD.example/api/v1'. Flavor.dev and Flavor.staging both return the real staging host https://level-up-backend-staging.up.railway.app/api/v1 (app_config.dart:43-44). The source carries its own TODO(contract) saying "Do NOT ship a prod build until this is replaced."
findings.interpretation: A production build is functionally impossible today — every request would fail DNS. Worse is the adjacent failure mode: lib/main.dart forwards to main_dev.dart, so any release build that omits -t lib/main_prod.dart compiles the LIVE STAGING URL into a production-signed artefact. docs/RELEASE_SIGNING.md records that this exact mistake already happened once (2026-09-05).
findings.recommendation: Replace the placeholder when the production host is published (it arrives via contract-changelog.md). Until then, treat any release artefact as staging-pointed. Consider making Flavor.prod throw at AppConfig.init rather than returning an unusable string, so the failure is at boot, not at first request.
findings.exploitable: Not exploitable by a third party. It is a release-correctness and data-routing defect.

findings.title: Legal / privacy-policy URLs are reserved-TLD placeholders
findings.observed_fact: Three constants — _termsUrl = 'https://levelup.example/legal/user-agreement', _privacyPolicyUrl = 'https://levelup.example/legal/privacy', _cookiePolicyUrl = 'https://levelup.example/legal/cookies' — are opened with launchUrl(..., LaunchMode.externalApplication) at line 118. A TODO(legal) on line 41 flags them as placeholders. .example is an IANA-reserved TLD that cannot resolve.
findings.interpretation: The only privacy-policy link a user can reach from inside the app is dead. Both Apple and Google require a reachable privacy policy for an app that collects minors' PII (this app collects date of birth, school and governorate). This is a store-submission blocker, not merely cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Publish the three documents and replace the constants before any store submission. Because the links are already wired and launch externally, the change is a constant swap with no UI work.

findings.title: Neither git hook is installed — the local enforcement layer is inert
findings.observed_fact: git config --get core.hooksPath returns nothing at local, global and system scope. .git/hooks/ contains only the 14 stock *.sample files. .git/config has no [core] hooksPath entry. Both hooks document the one-time install step (git config core.hooksPath .githooks) in their own headers; it has not been run in this clone.
findings.interpretation: pre-commit (format + analyze on staged Dart) and pre-push (the full tool/validate.sh gate) have never fired here. Combined with RISKS.md R-3 ("CI has never been observed running") and the fact that the two strongest CI jobs are gated to a stale main (see SEC-04), the ONLY validation actually executing is a human or agent manually invoking tool/validate.ps1. The documentation describes a three-layer gate; one layer is running.
findings.recommendation: Run git config core.hooksPath .githooks in this clone, or add an install step to the onboarding docs and a guard test that fails if the hooks are documented but not installable. Note the hooks are deliberately bypassable (--no-verify, LEVELUP_SKIP_HOOKS=1) by design — that is fine; silently-not-installed is not.
findings.exploitable: Not exploitable. Creates false confidence that quality gates ran.

findings.title: The two strongest CI jobs are gated to `main`, which is 8 commits stale
findings.observed_fact: codegen-drift and build-release-apk both carry if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'. Active development is on branch merged (HEAD e4d1401, 8 ahead of origin/merged); main sits at e71e9a1. The release-APK job is also the ONLY place the merged-manifest INTERNET permission is verified against a real built artefact (ci.yml:384-414).
findings.interpretation: The codegen-drift safety net and the release compile gate — including the aapt2 verification of the Tier-0 C-1 regression — have effectively never run against current work. The cheap grep half of the C-1 guard does run on every PR, but the audit's own comment says that half is "the cheap deterministic half" and the artefact inspection is "the only one that is actual proof."
findings.recommendation: Either extend the two if: conditions to include refs/heads/merged, or merge merged into main regularly so the gates see current code. This is a one-line change in each job.

findings.title: R8 / ProGuard is disabled for Android release builds
findings.observed_fact: The release buildType sets only signingConfig. There is no isMinifyEnabled, no isShrinkResources, and no proguard-rules.pro anywhere in android/. The Android Gradle Plugin default for minifyEnabled is false.
findings.interpretation: Release APK/AAB ships with unshrunk, unobfuscated Kotlin/Java. For a Flutter app most logic is in AOT Dart (already opaque), so the security benefit of R8 is modest — but the size benefit is real, and unshrunk resources compound the 1.83 MB font payload (ASSET-01).
findings.recommendation: Evaluate enabling isMinifyEnabled = true with isShrinkResources = true and a proguard file, then re-run the release compile gate. Do not enable blind: several plugins here (screen_protector, flutter_secure_storage) use reflection-adjacent paths and need keep rules. NEEDS HUMAN DECISION.
findings.exploitable: Potential only — increases reverse-engineering convenience, does not itself expose data.

findings.title: `Bash(python -)` is a standing arbitrary-code-execution grant in the local Claude settings
findings.observed_fact: permissions.allow contains 20 entries, all scoped. One is Bash(python -), which pre-approves executing arbitrary Python read from stdin. Another is Read(//f/level/**), granting read across the whole F:\level tree rather than just this repository. No token, key or credential is present in the file. The Windows username musta appears in several literal paths.
findings.interpretation: No blanket Bash(*) or skip-permissions setting exists, so the posture is broadly sound. Bash(python -) is the one entry that grants unbounded execution — a pre-approval that cannot be reasoned about from the rule text. The file is untracked (gitignored), so it does not ship.
findings.recommendation: Narrow or remove Bash(python -). Consider narrowing Read(//f/level/**) to the repository root. Leave the file untracked.
findings.exploitable: Potential only, and only within an already-trusted local agent session.

findings.title: CI actions are pinned to mutable tags, including a third-party action
findings.observed_fact: actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, actions/setup-java@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4 and subosito/flutter-action@v2 are referenced by floating major tags, not commit SHAs. subosito/flutter-action is community-maintained, not GitHub-owned.
findings.interpretation: A tag is mutable; a compromised or re-pointed tag executes in the workflow. Mitigations present and real: the workflow uses pull_request (not pull_request_target), declares permissions: contents: read, consumes no secrets at all, and uploads no artefacts except golden failure PNGs. Blast radius today is therefore low.
findings.recommendation: Pin to full commit SHAs with a comment naming the version, at minimum for subosito/flutter-action. Revisit before any signing secret is ever added to the workflow — at that point this becomes HIGH.
findings.exploitable: Potential only. No secrets currently reachable from CI.

findings.title: Gradle wrapper is gitignored and absent from the repository
findings.observed_fact: android/.gitignore ignores gradle-wrapper.jar, /gradlew and /gradlew.bat. All three exist on this machine but are untracked. gradle-wrapper.properties IS tracked and pins gradle-8.14-all.zip over HTTPS, but declares no distributionSha256Sum.
findings.interpretation: A fresh clone has no wrapper — builds depend on the Flutter tool supplying Gradle, which works but removes the version pin's teeth and makes 'reproduce the build' machine-dependent. The missing checksum means the distribution is trusted on transport security alone.
findings.recommendation: Consider tracking the wrapper (the standard Gradle recommendation) and adding distributionSha256Sum. NEEDS HUMAN DECISION — the current arrangement may be deliberate.

findings.title: Golden regressions can merge without failing CI
findings.observed_fact: The goldens job runs on windows-latest with continue-on-error: true. Its own comment says: "ADVISORY ... until it has been green once — flip continue-on-error to false at that point and add it to branch protection." That flip has not happened. The Linux gate runs --exclude-tags golden. All 41 baselines and all 7 golden test files were verified present and correctly tagged.
findings.interpretation: 41 pixel baselines across light and dark canvases exist and are correct, but nothing in CI enforces them. Locally tool/validate.* DOES run them (no tag exclusion), so the gate exists only on the developer machine — which is also the machine where the hooks are not installed (SEC-03).
findings.recommendation: Flip continue-on-error to false once the Windows job has been observed green, and add it to branch protection, exactly as the file's own comment prescribes.

findings.title: Staging host is compiled into every dev and staging build
findings.observed_fact: _stagingBaseUrl = 'https://level-up-backend-staging.up.railway.app/api/v1' is a compile-time constant, taken verbatim from the contract's servers: block. Flavor.dev resolves to the same host.
findings.interpretation: This is a public identifier, not a secret — it is published in the contract. It is recorded here because it means any dev/staging artefact that leaves the team carries a reachable live backend address, and because isDev does not gate it.
findings.recommendation: No action needed while it matches the contract. If a separate dev backend ever exists, split the two flavors.
findings.exploitable: Not exploitable beyond disclosure of a host already published in the contract.

findings.title: `AppConfig.isDev` is declared but never read
findings.observed_fact: isDev is set to flavor != Flavor.prod and is referenced nowhere else in lib/ — the only other match is its own doc comment at line 42. Independently: lib/ contains ZERO occurrences of print(, debugPrint, kDebugMode or kReleaseMode.
findings.interpretation: Read positively: there is no debug-only behaviour to leak into production, because there is no debug-gated code at all. The field is dead weight rather than a risk. It is worth recording because a future contributor may reach for it assuming it already gates something.
findings.recommendation: Either wire it or delete it. Low priority. NEEDS HUMAN DECISION.

findings.title: No secrets found anywhere in the tracked tree — verified
findings.observed_fact: A pattern sweep across every tracked file for sk_live, sk_test, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, ghp_*, AIza*, xox[baprs]- and BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY returned ZERO matches in code, config, Gradle, plist, XML, PowerShell and shell files. Every token/secret/password hit is documentation prose in contract/openapi.yaml or an explanatory code comment. android/key.properties.example uses CHANGE_ME placeholders only. No *.jks, *.keystore, key.properties, .apk, .aab or .ipa exists anywhere in the working tree.
findings.interpretation: Secret hygiene is clean and the gitignore rules that keep it that way are correct and non-duplicated (android/.gitignore owns the signing patterns; the root .gitignore explicitly defers to it with a comment rather than repeating them).
findings.recommendation: No action. Preserve the split-gitignore arrangement.

findings.title: TLS handling is left at platform defaults — verified, and that is correct
findings.observed_fact: lib/ contains no badCertificateCallback, no HttpClientAdapter/IOHttpClientAdapter override, no SecurityContext and no LogInterceptor. Info.plist declares no NSAppTransportSecurity key (ATS defaults apply). The Android manifest sets no usesCleartextTraffic and no networkSecurityConfig. Zero http:// URLs exist in production lib/ code.
findings.interpretation: Certificate validation is intact on both platforms and cleartext is off by platform default. There is no certificate pinning — a deliberate, defensible choice for an app whose backend host is still moving.
findings.recommendation: No action. If pinning is ever added, it belongs behind a kill switch, not compiled in.

findings.title: Token storage, session teardown and backup exclusion are correctly implemented
findings.observed_fact: Tokens and device_id live only in flutter_secure_storage with iOS options first_unlock_this_device + synchronizable: false. Logout calls clearTokens() (tokens only) and never clear(), preserving device_id so session_superseded eviction still fires. SharedPreferences holds only theme mode and locale, with every read and write in try/catch. invalidateSessionScope drops 11 user-scoped providers on logout. Android sets allowBackup=false, fullBackupContent=false AND excludes all five domains from both cloud-backup and device-transfer.
findings.interpretation: This chain is unusually well-reasoned for a project at this stage. The shared-handset PII leak it was built to close (Tier-0 C-2) is closed with a single inventory function rather than scattered invalidations, and there is a discipline test that fails when a new non-autoDispose notifier appears without being classified.
findings.recommendation: No action. When adding any user-scoped provider, add it to invalidateSessionScope — the discipline test enforces this.

findings.title: iOS has never been built — no Podfile, no entitlements
findings.observed_fact: There is no ios/Podfile and no ios/Podfile.lock, and no *.entitlements file anywhere. Six plugins in use ship iOS pods (flutter_secure_storage, connectivity_plus, device_info_plus, url_launcher, screen_protector, shared_preferences). Debug.xcconfig and Release.xcconfig are identical one-line includes. CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY[sdk=iphoneos*] is the legacy string "iPhone Developer". Info.plist has no ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption key.
findings.interpretation: The Podfile is generated on the first macOS build, so its absence is strong evidence that iOS has never been compiled — consistent with a Windows-only development machine. Every iOS claim in the store-readiness documents is therefore SOURCE-level at best, never BUILD or ARTEFACT.
findings.recommendation: Treat all iOS findings as unverified until a macOS build exists. Add ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption before the first App Store Connect upload.

findings.title: Bundle identifiers and display names diverge across platforms
findings.observed_fact: Android applicationId = "com.levelup.level_up_app"; iOS PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.levelup.levelUpApp. Android android:label="level_up_app" — the raw package name is what appears under the launcher icon. iOS CFBundleDisplayName is "Level Up App" but CFBundleName is level_up_app. The Android gradle file still carries the flutter create TODO comment telling the developer to choose a unique application ID.
findings.interpretation: Two different reverse-DNS identifiers for one product, and an Android launcher label that shows a snake_case package name to students. Both are store-submission items.
findings.recommendation: Settle one identifier scheme, set the Android label to the product name (via a string resource so it can be localised), and remove the stale template TODO.

findings.title: `skills/RESTORE.md` documents a one-command restore that silently reverts a security-relevant instruction fix
findings.observed_fact: diff -rq .claude/skills skills reports 6 differing files plus skills/RESTORE.md (only in skills/). md5sum over all 22 SKILL.md pairs: 16 identical, 6 differ. The 6 differences are one consistent edit: .claude/skills/ was corrected for adr-049 §3 (purchase-silent) on 2026-09-05; skills/ still teaches an external Paymob web checkout via url_launcher and a Fawry pending subscription state with its own "Payment processing" UI. skills/RESTORE.md calls the tree "a byte-identical mirror" and gives Copy-Item -Recurse -Force skills\* .claude\skills\. All 26 files under skills/ are git-tracked (verified: git ls-files skills | wc -l = 26), swept in by commit f987f20 whose message never mentions skills.
findings.why_misleading: An agent recovering a wiped .claude/ — precisely the scenario RESTORE.md anticipates — would follow the documented command on the file's own authority. The "byte-identical" claim suppresses any instinct to diff first. The result reinstalls instructions to build a paywall the contract deleted, in a repo whose top-level rule is that the contract wins.
findings.recommendation: Delete skills/, or replace RESTORE.md's body with a pointer to git history and remove the copy command. If the mirror is kept for a real reason, make the restore step a diff-then-review, and correct the six files. DO NOT run the documented command.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md — every headline number is wrong, and it cites a contract pin two re-vendors stale
findings.observed_fact: §1.1 asserts 63 commits (actual 112), ~36k lines of lib/ (actual 51,191), 849 passing tests (actual 1,429), 12 day-briefs (actual 15), 29 documents in docs/ (actual 41), 27 audit reports in .ai/audits/current/ (actual 35 top-level, 55 including parts), and a design-gap register with 48 entries (actual 88, numbered #1–#88 with no gaps). §1.2 says "the pin has since moved to 184d6ec (3.0.0-m1)" — contract/SOURCE.md pins 768e67d / 3.22.0-m1, vendored 2026-09-20, via 2dca3c5 / 3.13.0-m1. §1.2 also claims "Days 00–7b cite 23f0535"; only day1, day7 and day7b cite any pin at all — seven of the nine briefs in that range cite none.
findings.why_misleading: This is the file loaded automatically at the start of every Claude Code session, and it instructs the reader to consume it "top to bottom" before touching code. An agent that trusts it starts with a 68% undercount of the test suite, a 83% undercount of the design-gap register, and a contract version that has been superseded twice — including by the delta that made getExplanation real and made three newly-stable operations FORBIDDEN to the app.
findings.recommendation: Re-ground every number against the repository, or — better — delete the numbers and point at docs/WAVE_STATUS.md and contract/SOURCE.md, which are current and maintained. A count in a hand-written file is a fact with an expiry date.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md references sections of itself that do not exist
findings.observed_fact: §1.7 says "expect a dirty tree — see §3.4, do not 'clean' it". §1.8 says "Do §14 (THE COOKIE). It is the migration's completion signal." §1.1/§1.5 reference §7 and §10.3. The file contains §1.1–§1.8 and then two unnumbered sections ("Quick reference", "The one command", "Non-negotiables"). There is no §3.4, §7, §10.3 or §14. Separately, the working tree is CLEAN (git status --porcelain returns zero lines), so the "expect a dirty tree" instruction is also factually wrong.
findings.why_misleading: A fresh agent is given a completion ritual (§14) that cannot be performed and four cross-references that lead nowhere, then told to expect a repository state that is not the current one. The likely cause is that CLAUDE.md was extracted from the longer tell_claude.md handoff (deleted per its own read-receipt protocol) without renumbering. An agent may reasonably conclude the file is truncated and go looking for the missing parts.
findings.recommendation: Either restore the referenced sections or strip the dangling references and the §14 instruction. Delete the "expect a dirty tree" line.

findings.title: The loaded skill tree teaches a snake_case @JsonKey bridge that ten model files explicitly forbid
findings.observed_fact: Three skills in .claude/skills/ — the tree Claude Code actually loads — instruct: "API uses snake_case; Dart uses camelCase — bridge with @JsonKey(name: '...') in the model, nowhere else", with a worked StreakPair/current_streak example in seif-api-contract. Ten model files in lib/ carry the same defensive doc comment: "Contract keys are already camelCase — NO @JsonKey(name:) bridge is needed and none must be added." The 2026-09-05 remediation that fixed the purchase-surface language in these same files did not touch this rule.
findings.why_misleading: seif-api-contract is the skill that fires on any API-touching work, and its copy-pasteable worked example is the most likely thing an agent reproduces. The result is a mapping layer that is wrong against the live contract, written into committed model code.
findings.recommendation: Delete or invert the snake_case instruction in all three skills. The ten doc comments in lib/ are the correct statement of the rule; lift their wording.

findings.title: The `bloc` skill specifies a quiz timer that does not exist and the code says so
findings.observed_fact: bloc/SKILL.md has a "Timer discipline" section specifying a QuizTimeExpired event, a QuizTimedOut state and an in-bloc countdown Ticker. Neither quiz_event.dart nor quiz_state.dart contains any such type. quiz_state.dart:94-97 states: "There is no timer and no timeout state. The bloc skill describes a countdown, but the contract defines no time limit on a quiz anywhere." Tracked as K-36 in known-issues.md; still open. The file is byte-identical in both skill trees, so this is not a mirror-staleness problem — it is a live defect in the tree that loads.
findings.why_misleading: The bloc skill is scoped to fire on ANY quiz work. An agent asked to touch the timer, the results flow or the answer path would build a fabricated event chain against a state machine that has none of it, then have to unpick it.
findings.recommendation: Delete the Timer discipline section (K-36 already prescribes exactly this). If a timer is ever specified, it needs a contract field first — seif_fight.md S7 is the open question.

findings.title: `docs/ASSET_MANIFEST.md` lists shipped assets as "still needed" and prescribes the wrong paths
findings.observed_fact: The manifest's "Still needed" table asks for five nav glyphs at assets/icons/nav_home.svg, nav_leaderboard.svg, nav_learn.svg, nav_message.svg, nav_account.svg. All five already exist — at DIFFERENT paths: assets/icons/nav/home.svg, nav/leaderboard.svg, nav/learn.svg, nav/message.svg, nav/account.svg, each referenced exactly once from lib/. It also asks for assets/icons/bell.svg; the repo ships assets/icons/notification.svg, in use. Other rows are still accurate — home_banner.png, level_medallion.png and assets/icons/profile/*.svg genuinely do not exist.
findings.why_misleading: Partial staleness is worse than total staleness: the reader cannot dismiss the document, so they trust the wrong rows too. An agent following it would create five duplicate SVGs at flat paths, add a second assets/icons/ entry to pubspec, and ship both copies — while the real ones stay wired.
findings.recommendation: Move the five nav rows and the bell row into the "Already downloaded" table with their REAL paths. Keep the genuinely-outstanding rows.

findings.title: Three files route agents to an off-repository Obsidian vault, one of which is declared wrong
findings.observed_fact: PROJECT_GUIDE.md's rule-precedence table places level_up/01_Flutter_Specs/ at level 4 ("Existing project architecture") and level 5 ("Project-wide engineering rules"). Its own source table then says of level_up/01_Flutter_Specs/Architecture_and_Folders.md: "⚠ known stale — wrong in 5 of ~10 assertions. The code is right in 4 of 5. Fix the doc." CLAUDE.md:70 repeats the warning. test/widget_test.dart:2 says "See the vault's Testing_and_Quality spec." No such path exists in the repository.
findings.why_misleading: The governance index — the file whose job is to say which source wins — sends the reader to a source that (a) is not in the repository and therefore unreachable to any agent, and (b) it simultaneously declares to be wrong in half its assertions. An agent that cannot find it may search, infer, or worse, treat the absence as permission to invent.
findings.recommendation: Either vendor the specs into docs/ or remove them from the precedence ladder entirely and delete the dangling pointers. A rule source nobody can open is not a rule source.

findings.title: `_AGENT_CONTEXT.md` states expired hard constraints with nothing marking them expired
findings.observed_fact: The file declares: "REPORT ONLY. Do not edit, create or delete anything under lib/, test/, android/, ios/, assets/, pubspec.yaml or analysis_options.yaml", and baselines itself at "branch dev, commit e3651e6". These applied to one ten-agent audit pass on 2026-08-11. Nothing in the file, its directory, or any pointer to it marks the constraints as spent. Current branch is merged at e4d1401, roughly 60 commits later.
findings.why_misleading: It is the first file an agent following any "read .ai/audits/current/ for context" instinct would open — the underscore prefix sorts it to the top. Read as live, it forbids writing code at all; read for its project shape, it reports 66 test files (now 112) and a branch that has not been the working branch since 2026-08-22.
findings.recommendation: Add a dated CLOSED banner at the top, or move the whole 2026-08-11 wave into .ai/audits/2026-08-11/ so "current" means current.

findings.title: `known-issues.md` is called the live fix queue but is a 2026-09-05 snapshot with closed items unmarked
findings.observed_fact: CLAUDE.md's Quick reference labels it "The ordered fix queue". K-0 (uncommitted 141-file reformat), K-1 (missing INTERNET permission) and K-2 (logout PII leak) are presented as an open Tier 0. K-1 and K-2 were closed by Wave 1 and independently VERIFIED in fable-wave1-verdict.md; K-0 is long moot. Several Tier-3 enforcement proposals have shipped (test/guards/rules.dart and workflow_test.dart exist and run) without being crossed off. K-36 is genuinely still open.
findings.why_misleading: An agent told this is the ordered queue will start at Tier 0 and re-investigate three closed bugs, and may 'fix' the INTERNET permission that is already present and CI-guarded.
findings.recommendation: Mark closures inline with the verdict file that closed them, or regenerate the queue.

findings.title: Two unrelated documents share the `D-NNN` decision namespace
findings.observed_fact: .ai/audits/current/decisions.md records D-1…D-9, the Wave-0 orchestrator's audit-methodology judgment calls. docs/DECISIONS.md records D-001…D-011, the project's product and architecture decisions (D-007 removed the subscription row; D-008 gated then un-gated the leaderboard). Neither file cross-references the other.
findings.why_misleading: "D-8" is ambiguous in this repository. A citation resolved against the wrong file produces a confidently wrong claim about what was decided.
findings.recommendation: Rename the audit file's IDs (e.g. AD-1) or add a one-line disambiguation header to both files.

findings.title: `wave3-implementation.md` contradicts `WAVE_STATUS.md` on whether Wave 3D is finished
findings.observed_fact: The implementation record self-reports 3D as "stopped, needs design input". WAVE_STATUS.md — which CLAUDE.md says wins every disagreement — shows 3D ✅ COMPLETE (2026-08-21), and the typography ratchet reaching 0 confirms it.
findings.why_misleading: Both files are in the agent's likely read path. The precedence rule resolves it, but only for an agent that knows the rule — and the implementation record is the more specific, more detailed-looking document.
findings.recommendation: Add a closing note to wave3-implementation.md: 3D completed 2026-08-21, ratchet at 0.

findings.title: `contract/SOURCE.md` flags a router defect that was fixed two days after it was written
findings.observed_fact: SOURCE.md (vendored 2026-09-20) states: "The leaderboard gate's comment at lib/core/router/app_router.dart:152-158 claims GET /leaderboard is 'x-stability: draft AT OUR PIN'. That was already false at 2dca3c5 and is false here." The current router at that location reads: "UN-GATED 2026-09-22. D-008 is closed: GET /leaderboard is x-stability: stable at the pin 768e67d (3.22.0-m1, contract/openapi.yaml:2007)…" — fixed by commit 09dca36.
findings.why_misleading: contract/ is a DO-NOT-EDIT vendored directory, so the stale note cannot be corrected in place without breaking that rule. An agent following SOURCE.md's remaining-work list would go 'fix' code that is already correct.
findings.recommendation: Record the discharge in docs/DECISIONS.md under D-008 and in docs/WAVE_STATUS.md, and leave contract/ untouched. This is a case where the vendoring rule and the accuracy rule genuinely conflict; the resolution is a note outside contract/.

findings.title: `README.md` is the untouched `flutter create` template
findings.observed_fact: 571 bytes, verbatim boilerplate: "# level_up_app / A new Flutter project. / This project is a starting point for a Flutter application." pubspec.yaml carries the matching description: "A new Flutter project.". The repository has 112 commits, 51,191 lines of lib/, 1,429 tests, 41 documents, 22 skills, a vendored API contract and three prior audits.
findings.why_misleading: README is the file every human and most agents open first, by convention, before CLAUDE.md. It describes a scaffold. Both prior audits already flagged it (flutter_project_audit.html; .ai/…/06_security_release.md SEC-15) and it has not been acted on in seven weeks.
findings.recommendation: Write a real README: what the app is, the five entrypoints, tool/validate.*, and a pointer to CLAUDE.md → WAVE_STATUS.md → PROJECT_GUIDE.md. This is the single cheapest high-value fix in the repository.

findings.title: The `*_prompt.md` and `*_unblock.md` files read as live imperatives but are spent
findings.observed_fact: These are one-shot launch payloads: edit3_prompt.md opens "Copy everything inside the fence below into a fresh Claude Code session opened at F:\level\level_up\level_up_app." edit2_unblock.md says "Your job is to get into Figma…". All the work landed: f987f20 landed edit1/edit2, 7876242 landed edit3, e71e9a1 landed edit4 and edit5 and states "this closes the set." The three blocked items in edit2_unblock.md resolved the same day. Nothing INSIDE any of the three files says so. edit3_prompt.md and edit4_prompt.md are referenced by zero other files.
findings.why_misleading: Imperative prose addressed to a future agent, with no completion marker in the file itself, in the repository root where it is impossible to miss. The 'done' fact lives only in git history.
findings.recommendation: Move to docs/archive/ or add a one-line DONE banner with the landing commit. ARCHIVE, not delete — edit1–edit5 proper are cited by 40+ live code comments and must stay.

findings.title: Three large root-level artefacts are stale snapshots of this same repository
findings.observed_fact: flutter_project_audit.html (127 KB) is a previous full-project audit, "Generated 2026-09-08", header branch: merged @ 7e7129c (dirty) · contract: 184d6ec · 3.0.0-m1 · 88 commits, verdict "🟡 Fair — functional but incomplete", production-readiness score 22/100, 890 tests. flutter_code_tree.md (90 KB) self-declares "Generated 2026-09-19 from the source at HEAD 9f415dd" and still describes the leaderboard as gated. flutter_frontend_workflow.md (71 KB) is an application runtime trace dated 2026-09-08, also citing pin 184d6ec and 890 tests. None is referenced by CLAUDE.md, WAVE_STATUS.md, AGENT_WORKFLOW.md or PROJECT_GUIDE.md.
findings.why_misleading: Three authoritative-looking, large, root-level documents about this exact repository, all predating the elevation system (edit1–5), the 3.13 and 3.22 contract re-vendors, the Mistakes ship and the leaderboard un-gating. flutter_frontend_workflow.md additionally shares a name with the real process doc docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md — a search for "workflow" returns both. Note: they do not contain contradictory RULES; the inspection found zero quotable rule conflicts. The risk is stale FACTS presented with authority.
findings.recommendation: ARCHIVE all three under docs/archive/2026-09-08/ with a dated banner, or regenerate. Keep flutter_project_audit.html — it is the direct predecessor of this report and its "potentially useless files" section is still largely accurate.

findings.title: `WAVE_STATUS.md` — the declared source of truth — has no row for the elevation waves
findings.observed_fact: A grep of WAVE_STATUS.md for elevation, edit[1-5] and ratchet returns only unrelated typography-ratchet lines. Its Waves table goes from Day 10 (2026-09-12) straight to Leaderboard (2026-09-22), with no row for edit1–edit5 — despite both landing commits (f987f20 2026-09-19, e71e9a1 2026-09-21) predating its own "Last updated: 2026-09-22" stamp. Confidence is MEDIUM because the grep was keyword-based; a row under a different name may exist.
findings.why_misleading: CLAUDE.md says this file wins over every other document about wave state. An agent that reads only WAVE_STATUS.md would not learn that the entire Glass/elevation design system exists — while 32 live files in lib/ and test/ carry (edit1.md R#) citations in their comments.
findings.recommendation: Add the elevation wave rows. Verify the gap first — it is the one finding here I could not close to HIGH confidence.

findings.title: `test/widget_test.dart` is a trivially-true placeholder
findings.observed_fact: The entire test is test('scaffold boots', () { expect(1 + 1, 2); });, with a comment pointing at an off-repo vault spec. It touches no application code and would pass against an empty tree.
findings.interpretation: It is not worthless: it is the file whose silent omission motivated removing the hard-coded directory list from CI (workflow_test.dart now fails if a path argument is reintroduced). It functions as a test-discovery canary rather than an application test.
findings.why_misleading: A reader counting tests sees a passing test that proves nothing. A reader deleting 'dead' tests removes the canary.
findings.recommendation: KEEP — but rename it or add a comment saying it is a discovery canary, so nobody deletes it as dead weight.

findings.title: `.ai/audits/current/store_readiness_audit.md` is the newest, deepest audit and nothing points to it
findings.observed_fact: docs/STORE_READINESS.md names docs/STORE_READINESS_AUDIT_2026-09-05.md as the authority on facts. That 09-05 audit is superseded by .ai/audits/current/store_readiness_audit.md — "Status: FINAL v2", 2026-09-21→22, built against the current pin, with 20 supporting store_readiness_parts/ files and a full adversarial review cycle, committed in e683e8d. docs/STORE_READINESS.md contains zero references to it, to .ai/audits/current/, or to any 2026-09-2x date. CLAUDE.md's Quick reference points into .ai/audits/current/ only via known-issues.md.
findings.why_misleading: An agent following the documented pointer chain lands on a 17-day-stale document and never discovers the one that replaced it. The forward-pointer chain is broken at exactly the step that matters most for shipping.
findings.recommendation: Add a forward pointer in docs/STORE_READINESS.md and a Quick-reference row in CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: `mistakes_subject_card.dart` says Cairo is not in the design system; the theme and pubspec disagree
findings.observed_fact: The widget comment reads: "Frame: Cairo 600 / 14 … Cairo is not in the design system and adding a [family] …". app_theme.dart:54 sets fontFamilyFallback: const ['Tajawal', 'Cairo'], and pubspec.yaml bundles three Cairo weights (283 KB).
findings.why_misleading: A small, local contradiction about whether a font family is part of the system. An agent reading the widget would conclude Cairo is unavailable and work around it; an agent reading the theme would use it freely.
findings.recommendation: Reword the widget comment to say Cairo is a tertiary Arabic fallback, not a named style family.

findings.title: Mixed state management is INTENTIONAL, scoped and enforced
findings.observed_fact: Bloc exists only at lib/features/quiz/bloc/{quiz_bloc,quiz_event,quiz_state}.dart. Everything else is Riverpod. test/guards/project_rules_test.dart test 1 (blocOutsideQuiz) asserts this mechanically and passes. Both the bloc and river skills state the boundary identically and correctly.
findings.assessment: This is the textbook case of a mixed architecture being deliberate rather than accidental: one bounded context (a strict state machine with illegal-transition rejection) uses Bloc; the rest, which is server-data-shaped, uses AsyncNotifier. It is documented, guard-enforced and mutually consistent across the instruction layer. It should NOT be 'cleaned up'.

findings.title: Riverpod is the DI container — no service locator
findings.observed_fact: lib/core/providers/core_providers.dart defines secureStorageProvider, preferencesStoreProvider, refreshDioProvider, dioProvider, connectivityProvider, isOnlineProvider. No get_it or equivalent appears anywhere. dioProvider carries an explicit left-side type annotation to break a static reference cycle with authRepositoryProvider (the refresh closure is resolved lazily at onError).
findings.assessment: Clean, single-container DI. The cycle-breaking annotation and the lazy refresh closure are both non-obvious and both correctly commented.

findings.title: Two dead feature scaffolds and one dead route remain in `lib/`
findings.observed_fact: lib/features/subscription/ and lib/features/track/ each contain four .gitkeep files and zero Dart. 29 .gitkeep files are tracked overall; lib/features/home/{models,notifier,repository}/ are also empty. /track-select is a registered route (app_router.dart:135) rendering _Placeholder('Track select'); nothing navigates to it — the only two references to the string are the route definition and a doc comment at line 427.
findings.assessment: subscription/ is dead by DECISION, not neglect: adr-049 §3 made the app purchase-silent and D-007 removed the Profile subscription row. Keeping an empty subscription/ directory is therefore actively misleading — it implies a surface that the contract forbids building. track/ is dead because registration absorbed track selection. NEEDS HUMAN DECISION.

findings.title: `lib/dev/mock_backend.dart` cannot ship — proven by import graph, not by convention
findings.observed_fact: 2,124 lines simulating 17 endpoints with contract-faithful canned JSON. grep -rn "mock_backend" lib returns exactly one hit: lib/main_mock.dart:30. main_mock.dart is itself imported by nothing. None of main.dart, main_dev.dart, main_staging.dart, main_prod.dart, bootstrap.dart or app.dart reaches it. Dart tree-shakes from the entrypoint's reachable graph, so no shipping build can contain it. Exercised by 4 test files / 44 tests.
findings.assessment: A dev harness inside lib/ is a legitimate smell to check; here it is provably inert in production and the single dioProvider override is why no production file had to learn about it.

findings.title: Error handling is typed end-to-end with no silent swallowing on the network path
findings.observed_fact: ErrorInterceptor maps every DioException to a sealed AppException (OfflineException, NetworkException, ApiException, UnauthorizedException, ValidationException, RateLimitedException, UnknownException). Retry-After parsing accepts delta-seconds only and returns null on anything unusable rather than trusting the device clock. ProblemDetails.errors parsing degrades to {} rather than throwing. The only deliberate swallows are the three try/catch blocks in PreferencesStore, each with a written justification (a damaged preferences file must not prevent startup).
findings.assessment: One open TODO: error_interceptor.dart:8 — "full mapping of error-codes.md codes lands per-feature". Unmapped codes fall through as ApiException carrying the raw code, which is a safe default.

findings.title: Contract coverage: 26 of 43 declared paths are consumed; 3 stable paths are forbidden
findings.observed_fact: 43 paths are declared in contract/openapi.yaml. 26 are called from lib/. The 17 not called are: the four /auth/recovery/* paths; /auth/redemption-session/otp/{request,verify} and /subscription-codes/redemptions (all three x-consumers: [web] — FORBIDDEN to this app); /me/avatar; /me/fcm-token (newly stable, push not built); /me/notifications, /me/notifications/unread-count, /me/notifications/{id}/read; /me/deletion-request; /catalog/modules; /quizzes/{quizId} (draft — quiz history); /questions/{id}/favorite; /me/favorites; /leaderboard/me.
findings.assessment: At pin 3.22.0-m1 the rule "build only against x-stability: stable" became insufficient for the first time: three of the four newly-stable operations are web-only. stable must now be read together with x-consumers. This is the single most important contract-semantics change in the current delta and it is stated clearly in contract/SOURCE.md — but nowhere in CLAUDE.md's Non-negotiables, which still says only "Build only against x-stability: stable."

findings.title: Fonts are 85% of the asset payload; two Arabic families are bundled
findings.observed_fact: Total assets/ = 2,147,896 bytes. Fonts alone = 1,827,696 bytes (85.1%). Inter's four weights = 1,373,860 bytes (64% of ALL assets) at ~343 KB each. Cairo (3 weights) = 283,820 bytes and Tajawal (3 weights) = 170,016 bytes — both are Arabic families. app_theme.dart:54 sets fontFamilyFallback: const ['Tajawal', 'Cairo'], so Cairo is reached only for glyphs Tajawal lacks. Flutter tree-shakes ICON fonts but not text fonts.
findings.interpretation: Cairo is not dead — it is wired as a tertiary fallback — but 283 KB for a fallback-of-a-fallback is a real payload question, and one widget comment already claims Cairo is "not in the design system" (AI-19). Inter's 18pt static files are full multi-language builds; the app needs Latin plus punctuation.
findings.recommendation: Two independent options, both NEEDS HUMAN DECISION: (a) drop Cairo if Tajawal's coverage is sufficient for Egyptian Arabic — saves ~283 KB; (b) subset Inter to the Latin range — potentially saves several hundred KB. Measure before acting; do not remove a declared font without checking assets/fonts/README.md's warning that a missing declared font is a build error.

findings.title: Zero unused runtime assets — verified
findings.observed_fact: All 15 runtime SVGs (5 under images/, 5 under icons/, 5 under icons/nav/) are referenced from lib/. The three assets/launcher_icon/ files are build-time inputs, deliberately excluded from flutter: assets: with a written explanation. Two .gitkeep files hold otherwise-populated directories. No orphan images, no duplicate icons, no debug screenshots inside assets/.
findings.interpretation: Asset hygiene is clean. The largest single non-font asset, onboarding_illustration.svg at 185 KB, is a genuine full-screen illustration and is used.
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: 76 device-walkthrough screenshots sit untracked in `docs/device_pass/`
findings.observed_fact: docs/device_pass/ holds 76 PNGs plus ui_dump.xml, timestamped 2026-08-04, named for a Day-00 onboarding→registration→home walkthrough. The directory is gitignored with an explicit rationale ("a single pass is ~12 MB of PNGs that git can never shrink again"). No .md file in docs/ references them.
findings.interpretation: Correctly ignored — the gitignore comment shows this was a considered decision, not an oversight. They are machine-local evidence for one debug session. They do not ship and do not affect the repository.
findings.recommendation: No repository action. The developer may delete them locally at any time. Findings worth keeping belong in DESIGN_ISSUES.md / KNOWN_BUGS.md as text, exactly as the gitignore comment says.

findings.title: `build/` holds ~258 MB of stale compiler caches
findings.observed_fact: build/ contains three *.cache.dill.track.dill files of 86–92 MB each, dated July and early August 2026, plus per-plugin subdirectories. It is gitignored (/build/).
findings.interpretation: Normal, ignored, regenerable build output. Recorded only because it dominates the on-disk footprint and its age suggests nothing has done a full clean build on this machine since early August.
findings.recommendation: flutter clean reclaims it whenever disk matters. Never track it.
